analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, patches and supplied source excerpts against the indexed threat model and selected T-041 detail. The changes document broader media admission: GLM accepts variable-frame-rate tracks using presentation-order indexing and nominalFrameRate (docs/architecture/inference.md head 810–813); shared ingestion accepts mov/x-m4v labels while retaining byte-based MP4/QuickTime identification (head 1896–1899; changelog.d/glm-variable-frame-rate-video.md 3–4). No concrete regression is established by these documentation changes. The supplied patch retains the 512 MiB kept-frame cap, visual-token cap, deterministic processor refusals and GLM media exclusion from prefix reuse, relevant to A-001, TB-007 and T-041. No changed authorization, attestation, encryption, billing, credential or fan-helper behavior is evidenced. Extensive surrounding BASE documentation describes distinct Nemotron admission, decode bounds and cancellation; these unchanged contracts are not findings.
Integration should verify the actual GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset and MediaIngest/MemoryBackedVideoAsset changes: finite positive rate validation, bounded source-frame decoding despite VFR metadata, cancellation, request-wide memory reservations and container sniffing for the new labels. Also confirm the expanded formats preserve memory-backed plaintext handling (T-050) and do not widen cache participation (T-041). Those implementations and tests are not supplied in this batch, so documentation alone cannot establish their controls or a vulnerability. Remaining uncertainty concerns the newly admitted media's resource and plaintext lifecycle, not unrelated unchanged dependencies.
